earlier_scan.source_named: Bai, Bibo & Xu, Xianming. 2015. [Description of Cosao, a newly discovered Bi-Ka language of the Laos-China border] (cited on Glottolog cosa1234; not found online)

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2016. The classification of Cosao (slide deck). Same Zenodo record.

Hsiu, Andrew. 2016. The classification of Cosao: a Lolo-Burmese language of China and Laos. Handout (11 pp.) and slides, 22nd Himalayan Languages Symposium, IIT Guwahati, 8-10 June 2016. Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.1127810.
sources.note: Nothing. Comparative-lexical classification paper; Cosao forms are cited with Chao tone numbers (e.g. tsʰo55 sɔ55, u31 kʰja31, mja33 sɯ53), notes two sound correspondences with Khir (Cl- : Cj-, -ŋ : -m); no word on stress or accent.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. Southern Loloish lexical database (SouthernLoloish.xlsx, in Zenodo record 1127810) - Cosao column keyed from Bai 2015.
sources.note: Open; contains ~300 Cosao lexical items with tones copied from Bai 2015 - useful to confirm the tone inventory, but will not contain a stress statement.

sources.citation: Bai, Bibo & Xu, Xianming. 2015. Documentation of endangered Cosao "green codes" in Yunnan, China. Slides presented at the 4th International Conference on Language Documentation and Conservation (ICLDC), Honolulu, 27 Feb 2015.http://hdl.handle.net/10125/25306
sources.note: Nothing. Ethnobotanical 'plant code' talk; states only that Cosao is a Southern Yi (Loloish) Tibeto-Burman language without writing; a few plant names given with tone numbers (sɯ31 ho).

sources.citation: Bai, Bibo & Xu, Xianming. 2015. Description of Cosao, a newly discovered Bi-Ka language of the Laos-China border. (Paper cited by ELCat/Glottolog for cosa1234; apparently unpublished manuscript submitted to the Endangered Languages Catalogue.)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: English-language sketch by the same authors cited by ELCat; if it circulates it would likely contain a short phonology section with the tone inventory and any remark on stress. Not found online; ELP page 10709 is behind an automated-access block.

sources.citation: Bai, Bibo 白碧波 & Xu, Xianming 许鲜明. 2015. 搓梭语研究 [A study of Cosao]. Beijing: 民族出版社. 4+437 pp. ISBN 9787105138913.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only first-hand description of Cosao (Glottolog listed by Glottolog as a grammar; Grambank's sole source). Chapter 2 语音 will give 声母/韵母/声调 and, if anything is said about stress or weak (轻声) syllables, it will be there. Not in HathiTrust, archive.org, or any open repository; print only (Douban/JD list copies for sale).

sources.citation: 白碧波, 陈丽云, 许鲜明. 2018. 搓梭人植物暗语及其隐喻文化研究 [The Cosao people's plant codes and their metaphor culture]. 玉溪师范学院学报 2018(1). NCPSSD id 7000454657.

sources.note: Abstract read on NCPSSD: about plant-message codes (homophony, metaphor); not a phonological description.
